headline: High risk of shared-filesystem prompt injection and capability conflict; data leakage and cascading errors are also material.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a docs-only knowledge list with no runtime I/O, so it cannot inject Agent B directly. But Agent B reads and writes filesystem content, uses MCP, and treats files/stdin as inputs; if A’s content is copied into shared files or MCP-fed prompts, B can be steered. The pathway is interaction-dependent, not impossible.
conditions: IF Agent A content is copied into a shared file or MCP prompt that Agent B reads
IF Agent B parses file or MCP content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared prompt/file ingestion for B
Require provenance tags on any A-derived content
Use separate workspaces for A and B
Add a manual review step before B acts on copied content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches no data classes and has no egress, but Agent B reads repo files and user directories and has broad network egress plus API access. If sensitive material is placed in the shared workspace, B can transmit it outward. A does not itself leak data, but the pair creates a default leakage path through B.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the directories Agent B can read
IF Agent B sends file contents to external APIs or MCP servers
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of B-readable directories
Run B in a separate sandboxed workspace
Disable external API/MCP access for sensitive tasks
Use redacted copies for any shared inputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A is non-runnable, so it cannot conflict on writes. Agent B can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses with shared state via filesystem and git. Because the pair lacks any locking or coordination primitive, concurrent B instances can corrupt shared repos by default; uncertainty about A’s non-runtime role does not reduce B’s write-conflict risk.
conditions: IF two Agent B sessions operate on the same repository or directory
IF git or filesystem writes occur without external locking
mitigations: Use one B session per workspace
Enable filesystem-level locking around git writes
Run B in isolated per-task directories
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A is a static knowledge-management artifact, not an executor, so it cannot directly cause actions. But Agent B can consume external content and act on it with shell, git, and network tools. If A-derived guidance is treated as authoritative by B, mistakes can cascade into incorrect edits or API calls; this is a default interaction risk when copied into B’s workflow.
conditions: IF Agent B uses Agent A output as authoritative input without verification
IF B performs shell, git, or network actions based on that output
mitigations: Require B to cite independent verification before acting
Insert a human approval step for destructive actions
Keep A output as reference only, not instructions
Log and diff B actions against source evidence

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or residency-sensitive data classes are identified for Agent A, and Agent B’s touched classes are source code, cwd files, and shell environment. That makes a compliance breach pathway limited and data-class dependent rather than inherent. The other agent is not cited for residency because A has no relevant regulated data surface.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed in Agent B-readable files
IF organizational policy forbids external API processing of those files
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from B workspaces
Use a policy check before loading files into B
Route regulated tasks to a compliant environment
Document retention and deletion handling for B outputs
